# lexo.cool

> Personal site of Lexo Liu, a CS undergraduate studying in the US, from Hangzhou, who has written Rust for 6 years. The site is a Windows 95 virtual machine running Netscape Navigator 3.0 in the browser.

## Viewing the site

- https://lexo.cool/ runs the v86 x86 emulator (WebAssembly) in the page. It needs JavaScript; pressing the power button starts Windows 95 with Netscape on the home page.
- The machine draws to a canvas: its pages can be seen in a screenshot but not extracted as text.
- Without JavaScript the page shows a text summary of the home page. That summary is current, not an older version of the site.

## Inside the machine

- Home page (http://lexo.cool/ in Netscape): introduction, projects, about and photo album pages.
- GitHub reader: http://github.com/OWNER/REPO in Netscape browses any public repository, its README and source files, rendered from GitHub's API.
- Wikipedia reader: English Wikipedia articles and search, rendered from Wikipedia's API.
- Hacker News reader: front page, threads and user pages, rendered from the Hacker News API.
- The desktop and Netscape's bookmarks open WaterUI, the Linux kernel and Rust (rust-lang/rust) in the GitHub reader, Hacker News and Wikipedia. Links to other sites open in the visitor's own browser.

## Projects

- [WaterUI](https://github.com/water-rs/waterui): cross-platform reactive GUI framework in Rust
- [May](https://github.com/May-Agent/may): agentic runtime and workspace orchestrator
- [Skyzen](https://github.com/zen-rs/skyzen): fast, type-safe async HTTP framework in Rust
